content.text: Both proteins fall under family 100905 ("Designed trimeric coiled-coil"). I'll fetch the next ancestor to confirm the fold/superfamily context.

answers.answer: Yes, within SCOPe 2.08 they are placed in the same family, so SCOPe treats them as homologous at the family level, but only as a classification-level statement about designed proteins. d1s9za_ (sunid 98768, sccs k.40.1.1, from PDB 1s9z chain A) and d1hqja_ (sunid 61142, sccs k.40.1.1, from PDB 1hqj chain A) share sccs k.40.1.1. Their ancestry runs through different protein nodes that both sit under family sunid 100905 'Designed trimeric coiled-coil' (sccs k.40.1.1), within superfamily sunid 100904 'Designed trimeric coiled-coil' (k.40.1) in class k (designed proteins). d1s9za_ -> species 'Synthetic' (103786) -> protein 'Amyloidogenic design-1' (103785) -> family 100905. d1hqja_ -> species 'Synthetic' (64668) -> protein 'Unnamed design-1' (100906) -> family 100905. Limits: the family placement reflects design-based architectural similarity within the designed-protein class, not descent from a common natural ancestor, so 'homologous' here should not be read as evolutionary homology in the usual SCOPe sense for natural proteins. It does not imply shared function, so the 'Amyloidogenic' label on d1s9za_ must not be transferred to d1hqja_ ('Unnamed design-1'). It also does not license using either entry as a template or sequence-homology proxy for the other or for natural proteins without independent sequence or structure evidence. The API confirms classification only, not the sequences or coordinates themselves.
